note: `v34handshak`'s rxstate 4 RECEIVE arm at 0x653e4, caught by build/test/t_v34hsrx4.  The arm is a retrain test, the TRN2 shift registers, the MP bit packer with its run-length half, the far end's J, and the tone detector with what follows it.  What the set has to prove is that each guard is driven from BOTH sides with the object's own constant and the object's own WIDTH -- 0x65427 is a 32-bit signed compare that no legal baud can separate from a 16-bit one, and 0x6cafd masks its COMPARE with 0x7fff while its STORE goes in unmasked -- and that each body's stores are the object's.  Ten of the fifteen exits write nothing of their own, so several claims here are caught only through the transcript or through the pairwise signature check.

TWO ANCHORS CARRY A LEADING NEWLINE AND ONE CARRIES AN ADDRESS, because the arm shares lines with the rest of the file.  `hs_setstate(obj, HS_MICROSTATE, V34HS_DET_SYNC)` appears three times in this arm alone and `t3c_txblock(obj);` appears in every arm in the file, so an anchor that is one statement long is finding 432's hazard by construction.  The repair is information rather than indentation: the enclosing statement, or the object address the source comment already carries.

why: EQUIVALENT THROUGH A SIXTEEN-BIT STORE, and the object's own width is what says so.  0x6a4c1 stores `%ax`, so only the low halfword of the product survives; reading +0x35a2 signed instead of unsigned changes the multiplicand by exactly 65,536, and 65,536 times any integer is zero modulo 65,536.  The trace at 0x6d26f is no help either -- its `cwtl` sign-extends the same low halfword.  So no value of +0xaa96 or +0x35a2 can separate the two readings.  The object's `movzwl` at 0x67b46 is a CODEGEN fact and is kept for that reason, which is CLAUDE.md's rule for a load whose signedness the compiler was forced to encode but no test can see.  `t_v34hsrx4.c` drives a descriptor of 0x8000 anyway, because the trace's own %d does separate signed from unsigned there and that mutation IS caught.

So the cached value and the reloaded one differ in bit 9 and nothing else, and 0x67b69's `and $0xfffffcff` clears bits 8 and 9 of whichever it is used.  The object reloads at 0x67b56 and this reconstruction does too, because that is what is there; it cannot be shown to matter.
